description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 as decision (c) of the byte-walk page (relayed verbatim by Make Distiller Fast: "a, b, c approved."; (c) was the recommendation to make this a separate follow-up with its own page).

Fold a def clause's projections onto the outcome edge, so a clause receives its values the way a case arm does: deletes the second read of the byte and leaves one dispatch lowering. 10 of the remaining 61 instructions per byte on the walk. Changes what the interpreter reads.

Needs its own proposal page with predictions before a builder.

comments.text: Measured before the page (MDF, develop 2eff1dec2, bench). (1) Walk probe whose body uses the matched byte (walk(<<c, r::binary>>, acc) when c < 128, do: walk(r, acc + c)), 140 MB: clause form 45.3 instr/byte, case form 37.4 (predicted 44-46 and ~10 fewer; held). (2) Distiller with the JSON decoder's 37 single-discriminant multi-clause functions hand-rewritten in case form (scratch; 81 JSON fixtures green on three paths; identical output): 84.63G -> 84.12G instr (-0.60%), 12.98G -> 12.85G cycles (-0.97%); predicted -2% to -5%, a miss. Cause: the decoder's per-byte loops bind a byte only for the guard and use only the rest in the body; an unused projection is already omitted and a rest is a cursor, so nothing is read twice there. The fold pays only where a body uses a value its guard or pattern already read. (3) Structure: def head and case share PatternDispatchPlan and subjects and diverge after it; the def form ignores the plan's bindings and rebuilds pattern variables as BackendClause.projections via bind_pattern, with its own code in native lowering, the interpreter (select_clause drops the Decided), artifact, runtime demand, semantic and keying: ~20 sites walk clause.projections. Not established: how a clause whose trimmed plan is a direct outcome (no dispatch) is fed. Value is concept removal, not distiller speed. Patch: MDF scratchpad b248/json-case-form.patch. Priority with the user (MDF suggests P3).

title: A clause receives the values its dispatch already read
